name: Innovation policy

subjectOf.text: Introducing a regulatory update where genuine regulatory reform is needed can deteriorate the relationship between regulation and innovation, because innovation driven by changing values and societal norms calls for reform rather than incremental updating.
subjectOf.abstract: If changing values and societal norms are driving innovation, calling for a regulatory reform, introducing a regulatory update where regulatory reform is needed can deteriorate the relationship between regulation and innovation
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation for Innovation (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2831040
scope_conditions: innovation driven by shifting values and societal norms

subjectOf.text: Rulemaking in the dynamic framework is an integral part of innovation that both supports innovation and curtails it, for innovation's own sake and for the maximization of societal welfare.
subjectOf.abstract: Rulemaking in the dynamic framework is seen as an integral part of innovation that supports the innovation but also curtails it for its own sake and maximization of societal welfare.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation for Innovation (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2831040

subjectOf.text: The obstacles preventing consumers and entrepreneurs from accessing a workable new technology are frequently not technological limits but human choices embodied in law: legal and regulatory rules prohibit or limit commercial exploitation of, and public access to, new technology.
subjectOf.abstract: These obstacles are not the result of technological limitations, but human choice. The law — and other regulations — can often prohibit, or otherwise limit, commercial exploitation of, and public access to, new technology.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531
scope_conditions: once the main technical problems of a technology have been solved

subjectOf.text: Because regulators seek to avoid grounds for criticism, they inevitably adopt an overly cautious posture, which is what the precautionary principle amounts to in practice.
subjectOf.abstract: Avoiding grounds for criticism inevitably results in an overly cautious approach, called the "precautionary principle."
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531

subjectOf.text: Regulatory caution produces a systematic disconnect between the regulation of an innovation and the commercial and consumer ability to access it.
subjectOf.abstract: The result is that, all too often, there is a disconnect between regulation and commercial and consumer access to that innovation.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531
scope_conditions: from the perspective of entrepreneurs and consumers

subjectOf.text: Regulatory caution is not neutral: it functions to reinforce the status quo, with the result that new technologies struggle to reach the market in a timely or efficient manner.
subjectOf.abstract: But such caution merely functions to reinforce the status quo and the result is that new technologies struggle to reach the market in a timely or efficient manner.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531

subjectOf.text: Lawmaking and regulatory design need to become more proactive, dynamic, and responsive.
subjectOf.abstract: Lawmaking and regulatory design needs to become more proactive, dynamic and responsive.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531

subjectOf.text: Law schools should educate lawyers who add value by helping clients and society adjust to the technological environment rather than lawyers who impose unnecessary or unwise restrictions on it, since such restrictions will not stop technological development anyway.
subjectOf.abstract: Law schools need to find ways to educate lawyers who can add value in helping clients and society adjust to our increasing technological environment rather than who will create unnecessary or unwise restrictions on it.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Legal Education in the Blockchain Revolution (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2939127

subjectOf.text: Regulators' relative unsophistication about the technology is itself a risk driver, because a poorly informed regulator is likely to over-react and precipitate new or expanded regulation.
subjectOf.abstract: The relative unsophistication of the regulators and the lack of regulators' understanding of the technology could result in an over-reaction which in turn can precipitate creating new / expanding existing regulations.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Blockchain-Based Securities Offerings (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411110
scope_conditions: regulators lacking technical understanding of blockchain

subjectOf.text: Regulatory uncertainty produces a chilling effect: because early adopters must apply traditional law to novel instruments and cannot reach a comfortable level of certainty, legacy businesses hold back from adoption.
subjectOf.abstract: As a result, there is a chilling effect over the industry where legacy businesses are weary to adopt because of regulatory uncertainty.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Blockchain-Based Securities Offerings (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411110
scope_conditions: current U.S. regulatory climate for tokens and digital securities

subjectOf.text: Regulatory sandboxes are an instance of regulatory decentralization: by lowering regulatory barriers and costs for testing disruptive technologies while protecting consumers, the regulator fosters innovation in increasingly decentralized products and services.
subjectOf.abstract: With the sandbox, the regulator aims to foster innovation by lowering regulatory barriers and costs for testing disruptive innovative technologies, while ensuring that consumers will not be negatively affected.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization and Feedback Effects (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808852
scope_conditions: based on the UK FCA sandbox introduced April 2016 and later ASIC, MAS, and FSRA sandboxes

subjectOf.text: Courts expanded software patentability without proof that it would increase innovation, and the result was that corporations filed and acquired thousands of software patents used to strategically undermine competitor projects.
subjectOf.abstract: What makes things worse, courts decided to increase the protections for software despite lacking proof that additional patentability of software would increase the level of innovation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859
